description: Run one read-only SELECT (DuckDB SQL) across the df_<id> dataframes that fdic_query_financials and fdic_get_deposits staged or an earlier register_as saved; joins, aggregates, window functions, and CTEs work. Before writing SQL, pass each table name to fdic_dataframe_describe to read its columns. DOUBLE columns come back as JSON numbers and dollar columns are thousands of US dollars; BIGINT results such as COUNT(*) come back as strings, so CAST them to INTEGER or DOUBLE for arithmetic. Writes, DDL, file-reading functions, and system catalogs are rejected. register_as materializes the result as a new dataframe with a fresh TTL.

preview.description: Rows to return inline (0–10,000); defaults to row_limit, and a value above row_limit is treated as row_limit. Set it low when register_as keeps the full result.

register_as.description: Materialize the full result as a new dataframe under this unused name (df_XXXXX_XXXXX: uppercase letters and digits). A name already staged fails as register_as_clash — including on a repeat of a call that already saved it. The live dataframes share a 1,000,000-row budget: the oldest are dropped to make room, and a result over the budget on its own fails as register_as_too_large. Omit to return rows only.

row_limit.description: Hard cap on rows materialized (1–10,000). A query matching more stops here and row_count_capped comes back true; use register_as to keep the whole result.

sql.description: One SELECT against df_<id> tables named in a dataset field or by fdic_dataframe_describe, up to 20,000 characters.

name: fdic_dataframe_query

cap.description: The cap that bound: preview when lower, else row_limit.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_unavailable`: DataCanvas is not configured in this deployment. `missing_table`: A table the SQL names is not staged — a df_ name that expired, was dropped to make room for newer dataframes, or is mistyped, or any other table name. `invalid_sql`: A SELECT fails to parse or prepare (syntax error, unknown column or function, bad expression). `sql_execution_error`: SELECT prepared but failed on the data. `non_select_statement`: The statement is not a SELECT, or cannot be parsed as one. `multi_statement`: The SQL holds more than one statement. `denied_function`: The SQL calls a file-reading or external-data table function such as read_csv or read_parquet. `plan_operator_not_allowed`: The query plan uses an operator outside the read-only allowlist (scans of staged tables, filters, joins, aggregates, set operations, sorts, window functions, CTEs, unnest). `system_catalog_access`: The SQL references a system catalog: information_schema, pg_catalog, sqlite_master, or a duckdb_*() function. `register_as_clash`: register_as names a dataframe that is already staged. `register_as_too_large`: The register_as result holds more rows than the staging budget (1,000,000 rows) allows on its own. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

expires_at.description: When the register_as dataframe is dropped (ISO 8601).

notice.description: Guidance when the query returned no rows or a cap withheld some.

registered_as.description: Name of the dataframe register_as created.

row_count.description: Rows the query produced, up to row_limit; with register_as, the exact count of the new dataframe.

row_count_capped.description: True when the query matched more rows than row_limit, so row_count is that cap.

rows.description: Result rows, bounded by preview and row_limit.

truncated.description: True when rows were withheld by preview or row_limit.

title: Query staged dataframes with SQL
